spec_family.name: New Construction Stair Riser & Tread Stain/Clear Coat
spec_family.description: Covers stain application, sanding sealer, and clear topcoat for stair risers and treads in new construction. Combined spec with coating_type dimension (stain_clear, stain_only, clear_only). Both risers and treads use EA as primary UOM. Anti-slip additive option for clear coat on treads. Material systems are product-role-based recommendations shared across all interior stain specs. Context prefix SRST avoids collision with STRS (paint counterpart SF_STAIR_RISER_NC).

includes: Stain application on bare wood stair risers (brush+wipe, roll+wipe, spray+wipe)
Stain application on bare wood stair treads (brush+wipe, roll+wipe, spray+wipe)
Sanding sealer application (0-2 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Clear topcoat application (1-3 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Anti-slip additive in clear coat for treads (optional, recommended)
Bare wood preparation (inspect, sand 120-150 grit, fill defects with wood filler, grain raise for waterborne, tack clean)
Wood conditioner application (softwood + stain, unless gel stain)
Tread nosing detail work (sanding and stain application on bullnose edge)
Interstage sanding between sealer coats (220-320 grit)
Interstage sanding between clear coats (320-400 grit)
Stain dry verification before sealer/clear application
Tread protection during riser work (tape treads during clear cure phases)
Landing/floor protection at top and bottom of flight
Wall masking along stringer edge (spray method)

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary configuration dimension — drives layer stack, material systems, and module activation.
configuration_dimensions.notes: stain_clear is the professional standard for stair stain work. clear_only for natural wood look or pre-stained surfaces.

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, and coat count defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT4 default for stairs (high-visibility, high-wear surface). QT3=budget. QT5=premium. Coat counts: QT3=2 total, QT4=4 total, QT5=6 total.

configuration_dimensions.description: Stain application technique. All methods include wipe step.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for stair detail work (nosing edges, riser-to-tread junction). Roll works for tread flats. Spray for production. All include wipe.

configuration_dimensions.description: Clear coat application technique. No roll option.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default. Spray for production. Roll PROHIBITED for clear coat. Lacquer requires spray.
Satin is most popular for stair treads (hides wear patterns). No sheen/QT gate for stain specs.
QT3 skips sealer. QT4 uses 1 coat. QT5 uses 2 coats.
Treads benefit from extra clear coats (high-wear surface). QT4 default of 2 coats is minimum recommended for treads.

configuration_dimensions.description: Anti-slip additive mixed into final clear coat for tread safety.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Recommended for treads. Polymer grit additive mixed into final clear coat. Does not affect sheen significantly but adds micro-texture for grip.

configuration_dimensions.description: Wood species grouping. Drives wood conditioner activation for softwood.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Hardwood is most common for stair treads (oak, maple, hickory). Softwood (pine) may be used for risers or budget treads.

paintable_items.name: Stair riser face
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each individual riser as one EA. Riser count from PaintScope Stairwell Geometry System. Standard flight = 12-16 risers.
paintable_items.notes: Vertical surface between treads. Small surface area (~2.2 SF per riser). Quick stain/clear application per unit.

paintable_items.name: Stair tread (including nosing)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each individual tread as one EA. Tread count = risers - 1 (top landing may not have a tread). Includes nosing edge.
paintable_items.notes: Horizontal walking surface. Larger than riser (~3.5 SF per tread). Nosing edge requires detail work. High-wear surface — extra clear coats and anti-slip additive recommended.

variants.notes: Standard stain+clear. 4 total coats. Professional residential standard for stairs.
Premium stain+clear. 6 total coats. Maximum durability for high-traffic stairs.
Production variant. Brush stain + spray clear.
Stain-only, no clear. Rare for treads (unprotected = fast wear).
Clear-only on natural or pre-stained wood. Common for hardwood treads showing natural grain.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of individual stair risers to stain/clear coat
Count of individual stair treads to stain/clear coat (typically risers - 1)
Wall masking LF along stair for spray method

protection_zones_required.condition: During riser work and between clear coats on treads
protection_zones_required.notes: Tape tread nosing edge during riser stain/clear to prevent drips. Between tread clear coats, protect cured coats from foot traffic with paper or light cover. NOT Ram Board — that is for the paint counterpart's heavy-duty protection.
Canvas drop cloths at landing areas. Stain drips are hard to clean.
Wall masking along stair run for spray method. Also when walls SS_PAINTED_*.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Stringer may be stained with same stain/clear. Routed to SF_TRIM_NC_STAIN.

valid_input_states.notes: Bare wood is primary input. clear_only also accepts SS_STAINED.

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Finished walls require masking for all methods.
Unfinished walls need masking for spray only.

site_condition_rules.effect: Landing floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Stair staining is typically one of the LAST interior NC tasks. Treads are the final stair component — stain treads after all other stair and stairwell work is complete to minimize traffic damage.
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Setup → Prep (sand, fill, grain raise, condition) → Stain risers → Stain treads → [Stain coat 2] → Stain dry → Sealer → Sealer interstage → Clear coat 1 → [Clear interstage → Clear coat 2] → [Clear coat 3] → Final inspect → Cleanup
sequencing_notes.internal_sequence: Risers before treads in each phase (work from top of flight down). This prevents stepping on freshly stained/coated surfaces.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Tread protection tape during riser work → Landing floor protection → Wall masking (spray) → Apply coats → Teardown
sequencing_notes.dry_times: Stain: 4-8 hrs (oil), 2 hrs (WB). Sealer: 2-4 hrs. Clear: 4-6 hrs (oil poly), 2 hrs (WB poly).
sequencing_notes.anti_slip_note: Anti-slip additive mixed into FINAL clear coat only on treads. Do not add to intermediate clear coats (creates rough surface for next coat adhesion issues).
sequencing_notes.notes: Stain spec is self-contained — no companion prime spec.

relationships.notes: Stain counterpart to SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Treads are commonly stained while risers may be painted — this spec covers the stain scenario for both.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC stair riser and tread stain/clear coat (Tier 3 in interior stain spec rollout). Key features: coating_type dimension, 2 paintable items (riser EA, tread EA), anti-slip additive option for tread clear coat, tread nosing detail work, risers-before-treads internal sequence, shared 9 material systems, 14 SOP modules, context prefix SRST.
